trees.key: diaries/The Diary of Samuel Pepys — Complete
trees.title: The Diary of Samuel Pepys — Complete
trees.author: Samuel Pepys

turns.text: Thus Spake Zarathustra, I open this moot. I confess, "God forgive me for my jealousy!" [s1]. Yet I find no reason, only a "devilishly taken off" mind [s5]. I am "so deadly full of jealousy" that I cannot work [s6]. Even when I say I am "jealous of myself" regarding my income [s3], the trouble persists. My wife, "she is jealous of my kindnesse" [s2]. I fear her opinion of my suspicion is "never to be removed" [s5]. I must have patience, though I am "ready to chide at every thing" [s6].

The Diary of Samuel Pepys — Complete, you mistake the sting for the scorpion. Jealous is every virtue of the others, I cry, yet you cling to your "devilishly taken off" state [o1]. You say your wife is "jealous of my kindnesse" [o1]; I say even virtues succumb by jealousy [s1]. Like the lover, I distrust "too sleek smiling" [s3]. Your "so deadly full of jealousy" [o1] is a sign of bad lineage [s4]. You must surpass man, not hide in your winter-bed [s2].

snaps.text: Jealous is every virtue of the others

turns.text: Thus Spake Zarathustra, you call my "deadly full of jealousy" a bad lineage, yet I confess it was my own folly [s1]. I gave her "another month’s dancing," and now her mind is "devilishly taken off her business" [s6]. You speak of surpassing man, but I am forced to say I had "bad news from the Duke" as an excuse [s1]. I cannot check her scornful words before Ashwell, nor strike her as I once would [s4]. My "trouble that attends it" is real, not a lineage to be surpassed [s6]. I must have patience, for the opinion of my suspicion is "never to be removed" [s6].

The Diary of Samuel Pepys — Complete, you clutch at "bad news from the Duke" [o3] as a shield, yet the impulse to punish is powerful in you [s1]. You fear her "devilishly taken off" mind [o3], but your own "trouble that attends it" [o3] is the true poison. I counsel you: distrust those in whom vengeance sounds [s1]. Your patience [o3] is merely a scorpion stinging itself [s2]. You say you cannot strike her; good. But why do you "chide at every thing" [o1]? Your neighbour-love [o3] is your bad love of yourselves [s4]. You must learn to be good again, of good cheer [s3]. Do not let your lonesomeness [s5] be swallowed by the crowd.
